# Allowlist for skills_validation_test.go.
#
# Format (one entry per line):
#   <skill rel path under skills/>|<exact claim text>|<justification>
#
# A claim is either a command reference ("forge <chain>") or a path
# reference exactly as the validator reports it. Use skill path "*" to
# allowlist a claim across every skill. Every entry REQUIRES a
# justification — unexplained entries fail the test. Entries whose claim
# no longer appears in the named skill fail TestSkillsAllowlistEntriesStillNeeded.

*|forge will not overwrite this file|canonical "yours" ownership banner text quoted in code blocks — prose, not a forge subcommand
forge/deploy/SKILL.md|forge env deploy --env|Counter-example, not a claim: the sentence exists to tell the reader the environment is a POSITIONAL arg — "`forge env deploy dev`, not `forge env deploy --env dev`". Deleting the wrong spelling would delete the correction.
forge/auth/dev-loop/SKILL.md|.forge/idp/pat.txt|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: the dev IdP WRITES this path on its first boot (forge sets it as ZITADEL_FIRSTINSTANCE_PATPATH, and .gitignore excludes .forge/*). The skill must name it because forge reads the credential from there when it registers the browser application, and a developer debugging a failed bring-up needs to know where to look.
forge/auth/dev-loop/SKILL.md|.forge/hostinfra/<name>/|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: a host-process mailpit keeps its message store (mailpit.db) in its entry's data directory, which defaults to .forge/hostinfra/<name>/ (internal/hostinfra Spec.dataDir, mailpit.go). .gitignore excludes .forge/*.
forge/observability/query/SKILL.md|forge env releases at prod|Real usage: `at <env> <timestamp|trace-id|duration>`, and every example's second positional (2026-10-21T14:05:00Z, a hex trace id, 2h) starts with a digit, where the chain tokenizer stops, so it sees one positional of the two ExactArgs requires. The verb and the env are checked; the forms are those of `forge env releases at --help`.
forge/architecture/SKILL.md|.forge/generate-hooks/<name>.log|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: every forge generate writes each generate hook's output there (generateHooksLogDir in internal/cli/generate_hooks.go), and a failing hook's report points at it. .gitignore excludes .forge/*.
forge/db/query/SKILL.md|.forge/audit/<env>.jsonl|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: every forge db query appends its audit record there (dbQueryAuditPath in internal/cli/db_query_audit.go), and the JSON output's audit.record names the file. .gitignore excludes .forge/*.
forge/deploy/lifecycle/SKILL.md|.forge/hosted-projects.json|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: forge writes the project's hosted bindings there the first time it deploys to a control plane (internal/cli/hosted_project.go hostedProjectBindingFile), and env teardown/--endpoint reads it. .gitignore excludes .forge/*.
forge/migration/ownership/SKILL.md|.forge/exclude-guard/<run>/|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: a generate run under scaffold.exclude backs up every file it restored there (generate_exclude.go backupRel), and the run's output names the directory. A user recovering a pre-run version needs to know where it is. .gitignore excludes .forge/*.
forge/migration/ownership/SKILL.md|.forge/orphans.json|Runtime artifact, not a scaffolded file: every full forge generate records the files no step produces any more there (generate_orphans.go orphansRel), and forge project prune --orphans reads it. .gitignore excludes .forge/*.
forge/shapes/SKILL.md|internal/app/roots.go|User-owned, never emitted: example `shapes` output for a //forge:root the reader declared themselves (the convention the architecture skill names, "internal/app, conventionally roots.go"). The fixture scaffold declares no root, so it cannot exist there.
forge/migrations/v1.0.0/composition-graph/SKILL.md|internal/app/roots.go|User-owned, never emitted: the file the reader writes their //forge:root structs into (the same convention as the architecture skill's "internal/app, conventionally roots.go"). The fixture scaffold declares no root, so it cannot exist there.
forge/migrations/v1.0.0/composition-graph/SKILL.md|internal/app/graph_compose.go|Emitted only in mixed mode: generate writes it (codegen.MixedComposeFile, internal/codegen/composition_graph.go) when a LEGACY composition has an adopt-marked root, which is the state this migration describes. The fixture scaffold adopts no root, so it never has one.
forge/migrations/v1.0.0/composition-graph/SKILL.md|pkg/config/roots_gen.go|Emitted only for a graph-mode project whose roots have a projected reach (GenerateRootsGo, internal/codegen/config_roots_go.go); the skill names it to say mixed mode does NOT project it yet. The fixture scaffold does not produce it, so it is absent there.
*|.forge/source-overrides.yaml|The machine-local cross-repo source override file: written by the developer (gitignored, never by forge), read by internal/gitsource.LoadOverrides
forge/migrations/v1.9.0/SKILL.md|forge fix tx-isolation|Removed in v1.9.0: the playbook names the codemod so a runbook that still calls it can find what replaced it (nothing; every project in the upgrade window is past its shape).
forge/migrations/v1.9.0/SKILL.md|forge fix harness-mocks|Removed in v1.9.0: the playbook names the codemod so a runbook that still calls it can find what replaced it (nothing; every project in the upgrade window is past its shape).
forge/migrations/v1.9.0/SKILL.md|(forge.v1.entity)|Removed in v1.9.0: the playbook names the retired option so a project still carrying it learns to delete it.
forge/migrations/v1.9.0/SKILL.md|(forge.v1.field)|Removed in v1.9.0: the playbook names the retired option so a project still carrying it learns to delete it.
forge/migrations/v1.9.0/SKILL.md|forge/pkg/approval|Removed in v1.9.0, and this playbook is how a project stops importing it: it names the package to find and copy out of an older release's module cache.
forge/vuln/SKILL.md|forge vuln show prod|Real usage: `show <env> <advisory-id|package>` takes two positionals, and every example's second one (CVE-2026-1234) starts with an uppercase letter, where the chain tokenizer stops, so it sees one positional of the two ExactArgs requires. The verb and the env are checked; the form is that of `forge vuln show --help`.
forge/vuln/SKILL.md|forge vuln exempt prod|Real usage: `exempt <env> <advisory-id> --reason … --expires …` takes two positionals, and the second (CVE-2026-1234) starts with an uppercase letter, where the chain tokenizer stops, so it sees one positional of the two ExactArgs requires. The form is that of `forge vuln exempt --help`.
forge/deploy/delivery-policy/SKILL.md|forge vuln exempt prod|Real usage: `exempt <env> <advisory-id> --reason … --expires …` takes two positionals, and the second (CVE-2026-0001) starts with an uppercase letter, where the chain tokenizer stops, so it sees one positional of the two ExactArgs requires. The form is that of `forge vuln exempt --help`.
forge/migrations/v1.11.0/sbom-vulnerabilities/SKILL.md|forge vuln exempt prod|Real usage: `exempt <env> <advisory-id> --reason … --expires …` takes two positionals, and the second (CVE-2026-1234) starts with an uppercase letter, where the chain tokenizer stops, so it sees one positional of the two ExactArgs requires. The form is that of `forge vuln exempt --help`.
